findings.summary: `athena plan` spends money and changes queue state by default.
findings.evidence: With the default budget of $2, `athena plan` runs model readings of underspecified unread requests, which marks them read and takes them out of the queue. The help and README document this, and `--budget 0` avoids it, but a reader would expect a command that 'prints the plan' to be read-only.
The test queues a request and inspects queue() without ever reading it, so it covers an unread job, not a read one.

findings.summary: I could not see the live non-empty `athena plan` output in this snapshot.
findings.evidence: `cargo run --bin athena -- plan --budget 0` ran as a nested run in a fresh scratch copy with fake agents and nothing queued, so only the 'nothing is open' path printed. The full output format is covered only by the stub-backed test plan_prints_order_groups_details_and_flagged_items_and_says_so_when_nothing_is_open.

summary: I'm passing this retry of hem1. Plan entries no longer get default values when they are built. Acceptance now comes only from explicit bullets in the request or from a reading's criteria; the request's first line is never copied in. The rung (which level of the requirements ladder the item serves) comes from the steward proposal that made the job, or is inferred from words and paths in the request or reading, or is flagged as missing. Open questions are now filled by looking things up: a touched path that does not exist, or a referenced job that is not in the records. In drain, the planning pass now reads unread requests whose plans are incomplete before it plans them, so a vague request is refused with a named reason and leaves the queue, and one that the reading makes specific runs without being read a second time. The new `athena plan` command prints the plan. Every new test I ran passed: 10 plan tests and 14 reading tests in athena-core (I picked them by name filter), and all 48 drain tests, including two that use the real step implementation. `cargo run --bin athena -- plan --budget 0` printed the empty-queue message and `plan --help` documents the command. I could only see the full non-empty output through the stub-backed test, because the snapshot runs as a nested run in a fresh scratch copy with fake agents and nothing queued. The docs, changelog and decision entry D105 cover what criteria 8 and 10 ask for. Only minor issues remain: `athena plan` spends money and changes queue state by default, and one test has a misleading name.
